issues.legal_issue: A conviction based on common intention cannot stand when the persons alleged to share that intention have been acquitted and the evidence does not establish that the accused shared an intention with the actual perpetrator or perpetrators.
material_facts: The accused was convicted of murder with the aid of common-intention liability, on the case that he acted in concert with four named co-accused.
The co-accused were acquitted, and the evidence relied on to show their presence, an exhortation, a guard, or weapons was rejected or unsupported.
The remaining evidence showed, at most, the accused’s presence after the victim had been struck; it did not establish prior concert or participation with the actual perpetrator or any other person.
issues.conclusion: The evidence could not support the required finding of common intention, so the conviction could not stand; the conviction and sentence were set aside and the accused was acquitted.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code requires proof, by direct evidence or legitimate inference, that the accused shared a common intention with the actual perpetrator or perpetrators. Where the case alleges common intention with identified persons and those persons are acquitted, the accused cannot be convicted on that basis unless common intention with the actual perpetrator or another person is independently proved. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_conviction and conviction_depends_on_shared_intention and alleged_associates_are_acquitted and not evidence_proves_shared_intention_with_actual_perpetrator

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal by a person convicted of a criminal offence.
predicates.conviction_depends_on_shared_intention: The conviction rests on the accused having acted with others who shared a common intention.
predicates.alleged_associates_are_acquitted: The persons alleged to have acted in concert with the accused are acquitted.
predicates.evidence_proves_shared_intention_with_ac: The evidence establishes that the accused shared an intention with the person or persons who actually committed the offence.

issues.definition: When a conviction in an appeal depends on shared intention with alleged associates who are acquitted, and the evidence does not prove shared intention with the actual perpetrator, the conviction cannot stand.

issues.legal_issue: Blood found on an accused’s clothing, when it establishes only presence at the scene after the crime, does not establish prior concert or participation in the crime.
material_facts: Human blood was detected at one place on the accused’s clothing.
The accepted evidence did not establish that the accused participated in the killing or acted in concert with the perpetrator.
The accused’s presence after the crime could be consistent with innocence, and the blood evidence could corroborate that presence only.
issues.conclusion: The blood evidence corroborated, at most, the accused’s presence after the crime; it did not corroborate prior concert or participation.
issues.legal_principle: For liability based on common intention under Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, evidence that merely corroborates presence after the crime does not prove prior concert or participation. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_conviction and blood_found_on_accused and blood_evidence_shows_only_post_crime_presence and not independent_evidence_proves_concert_or_participation

predicates.appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal by a person convicted of a criminal offence.
predicates.blood_found_on_accused: Blood is detected on an item of clothing or another article associated with the accused.
predicates.blood_evidence_shows_only_post_crime_pre: The blood evidence establishes no more than the accused’s presence after the crime.
predicates.independent_evidence_proves_concert_or_p: Evidence apart from the blood finding establishes that the accused participated in the crime or acted in concert with its perpetrator.

issues.definition: Where blood evidence shows only post-crime presence and independent evidence does not establish concert or participation, the blood finding does not establish common intention.

issues.legal_issue: A chemical examiner’s report of detected blood should provide the number and extent of stains where they can be described.
material_facts: The chemical examiner reported only that blood had been detected on an exhibit.

The report did not state the number of stains or their extent, although the court considered those details should ordinarily be reported unless the stains are too minute or numerous to describe individually.
issues.conclusion: A report that merely states that blood was detected is not sufficiently informative; chemical examiners should report the number and extent of stains unless they are too minute or numerous for detailed description.
issues.legal_principle: In criminal proceedings involving blood evidence, a chemical examiner should indicate the number of blood stains on each exhibit and the extent of each stain, unless the stains are too minute or too numerous to describe in detail. No statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this observation.

predicates.criminal_evidence_proceeding: The proceeding involves the assessment of forensic evidence in a criminal case.
predicates.chemical_examiner_reports_blood: A chemical examiner reports finding blood on an exhibit.
predicates.stains_can_be_described: The stains are not too minute or too numerous to be described in detail.

issues.definition: When a chemical examiner reports blood in a criminal evidence proceeding and the stains can be described, the report should state their number and extent.
